title: What If One Earthquake Shortened Every Day on Earth?

scenes.text: What if one earthquake sped up the whole planet? In 2011, Japan's did.
That quake, one of the strongest ever recorded, moved Japan's main island of Honshu about 8 feet, according to early USGS data.
NASA's Richard Gross calculated it shifted Earth's figure axis by about 6.5 inches, 17 centimeters.
It also sped up Earth's spin, shortening every day by about 1.8 microseconds.
The 2004 Sumatra quake did more, shortening the day by about 6.8 microseconds.
You could not feel it. But a few minutes of shaking changed how fast the whole planet turns.
